questions.q: What is an if-then sketch, as described in the summary?
a: A specific backup plan for what to do if a problem arises
A drawing that maps out your ideal career path
A short pitch you send to potential employers
A list of skills you want to learn next year
questions.why: The sketches go beyond imagining the worst case by deciding your exact response in advance.

questions.q: How do if-then sketches change the way you approach a risk?
a: You feel safer and more confident about moving ahead
You avoid taking the risk until it disappears
You delegate the decision to someone else
You focus only on the best possible outcome
questions.why: Knowing your next move in advance makes the risk feel manageable.

questions.q: What does the 100 People Project involve?
a: Sending a short offer to 100 potential contacts, such as a free consultation
Interviewing 100 people about their dream careers
Saving 100 dollars a week to fund a new business
Asking 100 friends to review your resume
questions.why: The project aims to get a side hustle off the ground quickly and start building customers.

questions.q: What does the 100 People Project help you practice?
a: Marketing skills, plus learning how you can best help people
Accounting and bookkeeping for a small business
Public speaking in front of large audiences
Negotiating salaries with future employers
questions.why: The messages may also bring in your first paying clients.

questions.q: What does the Gene Wolfe example show about careers?
a: You can pursue several passions over the course of a life
You should commit to one skill and master it fully
Creative work rarely pays as well as corporate work
Successful people usually change careers only once
questions.why: Wolfe kept writing a page a day for decades alongside his other work.
